questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Apart from the general appeal of going on an exchange in the form of trying something new, I specifically chose Paris/France because I wanted to improve my French. I have also travelled a lot in Paris previously, and quite like the city. To be honest, the academic aspect was somewhat secondary, and I would recommend someone going on exchange for exclusively academic reasons to apply for this university

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall, I had an amazing experience and greatly enjoyed my time in the city. The reason I am not doing a 10/10 is due to a few issues with the host university, administrative ones in particular.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Before arrival, I had set up an account on the university intranet (ENT) where info was communicated, but still things felt somewhat messy. A lot of info was sent to my personal mail in the first month

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Assistance mostly occurred by visiting the “Tolbiac” center, and presenting myself. There I received my study card, as well as some further information

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
First of all, I am not sure any "on campus housing" even exist.
I found housing in the Cité International Universitaire (CIUP). I am Danish, so I applied to the Danish house. I was given a spot, but due to the "brassage" system of the Cité, I ended up staying in the Belgian house.
I believe the Danish house had around 45 rooms available with 90 applicants, so make of that what you want.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I personally enjoyed living away from uni, with about a 35 minute walk each morning. The CIUP was a great place to stay and connect with people from all around the world.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I loved the housing I found, but could totally see it being horrible if I didn't succeed in getting into the CIUP

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A big mess, see below for further info

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
When I arrived in Paris, I already had my learning agreement approved from Copenhagen, as sending an approved learning agreement was part of the requirements for online registration.
However, during the intro week, we were send course schedules which A: weren't finished and B: showed that some of the courses from my original learning agreement took place at the same time. Due to this, I had to scramble in order to find a replacement course, reaching out to professors to send course descriptions (that were never available in the first place).
Eventually, once I had found a new course package, I was told to send the learning agreement to the international coordinator of the faculty to receive a signature, to then send the signed document to the Erasmus coordinator.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Communication was very loose, and I felt very much left to my own. Fortunately, communication with UCPH was much easier, and quite understanding of the messy situation

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I eventually managed to get everything aligned and get the courses I wanted, but the whole process was incredibly messy, and could have been so much easier if the university shared course descriptions and planned the schedule sometime earlier than the week before courses start

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Take a deep breath, and prepare for the worst.
Make sure to keep in contact with UCPH and start trying to get the info you need from Sorbonne as early as possible. Expect things to go wrong and lots of frustration, but also know that if you pay attention and keep working to solve things, eventually everything should be okay.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Plenty of interesting courses, but a rather limited selection in English. You have to be ready to study in French, as you can only get ~15 ECTS' in English.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Somewhat below the level I am used to at KU. Notably, courses in English felt quite a bit easier than those in French. Some of this may be due to me being much more at ease with English, but it also seems the academic ambition of the English courses has been lowered in order to allow for a more comfortable environment for the French students to practice their, often lackluster, English.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style varied a lot from course to course, but overall felt less participatory than that of UCPH. Not all professors used slideshows, and not all who did shared them after classes

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Médias et compétitions politiques
Issues of Climate change
Dimensions numériques du politique
Opinion et élections
France and the EU
Politiques économiques européennes

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend "Médias et compétitions politiques", mainly due to Mr. Simon who taught the course being a very engaging lecturer - you could clearly feel he cared about the subject.
I would also recommend "France and the EU", as it was fun to get a distinct French perspective on the EU, and quite approachable due to being in English

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not any really

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries were surprisingly manageable, but perhaps anything will seem fine when you're used to Copenhagen

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
An intensive French course was offered for the intro week. It was really useful, enjoyable, and I ended up making many friendships here.
Different social activities were also available, but communication was somewhat poor, and I didn't really make use of them

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend the intro week French course, great way to meet other exchange students and improve your French

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Just enjoy the city, it's Paris, there's something for everyone

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I guess it depends on what you consider culture to be. If we're talking administrative systems, I never adjusted, but everything else felt quite easy to get used to.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I know it may seem obvious, but speaking French. A lot of the locals are not that great at English, and will find it much easier to socialize with you if you do it in French. But also, you have plenty of opportunities to socialize with other exchange students in English

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: ADMINISTRATION/BUREAUCRACY

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I just really loved being immersed in the language, and getting to improve myself.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Prepare for hell in terms of administration/bureaucracy
2. Make sure to go to the intro week French courses and make connections
3. Enjoy the city, you are in one of the most exciting places in the world

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Most courses are graded using 2-3 different tests in the form of hand ins, presentations, multiple choice tests, etc. This allows a quite comfortable process, where you have a general sense of whether you will pass or not and can adjust your effort accordingly. But the course "Dimensions numériques du politique" had a professor who chose to ignore the general guidelines, and do the entire grade through one single written essay, taking place over two hours, in hand, in French. If you feel like that would be too challenging, avoid this particular course.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making new connections with people from all around the world and feeling how my French improved

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Repeating myself here, but the uni admin was horrible, prepare for the worst.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
